source_title: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems

standard_prerequisites.name: Partial Steiner triple system
standard_prerequisites.statement: A finite structure with a partial operation whose defined products are the blocks.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure whose predimension is computed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Unconfined configuration
standard_prerequisites.statement: A finite configuration is confined when it forces a product that is not already present; containing none is the hypothesis.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what allows an HF-ordering to exist.

standard_prerequisites.name: Predimension
standard_prerequisites.statement: The predimension delta of a finite system is the number of elements minus the number of blocks.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity shown to be monotone along the ordering.

core_obligations: Order the elements of the finite system increasingly, which the absence of a confined configuration allows, and write A_i for the initial segment of size i (source lines 405-408).

Compute the increment of the predimension when the next element is added, splitting into the case where it lies in one block of the enlarged system and the case where it lies in no block (source lines 408-410).
In both cases the increment is non-negative, so the predimension is monotone along the ordering and therefore non-negative at the end (source line 411).

proof_roadmap.step: Choose the ordering and set up the initial segments.
Case analysis on the number of blocks through the new element and conclusion by monotonicity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source line 402: the predimension of a finite partial Steiner triple system containing no confined configuration is non-negative. The author gave it no label, so its position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 404-412) introduces an increasing enumeration of the elements, which exists exactly because no confined configuration is present, and then computes the increment of the predimension at each step; the case split is on whether the new element lies in one block of the enlarged system or in none, and the increment turns out non-negative in both cases, so monotonicity along the enumeration gives the bound. The statement records only the sign of the predimension.
